title: What Do Uniforms Do to the Wearer—and the Observer?
scope_note: No evidence establishes one universal neurological or behavioral effect of uniforms. The sources support bounded claims about person perception, specific laboratory tasks, one workplace case and one small fMRI task.

sources.title: Dress Is a Fundamental Component of Person Perception
sources.limit: Dress contributes to inference; inference is not accurate knowledge and uniform-specific evidence remains sparse.

sources.title: What should I wear to work? An integrative review of the impact of clothing in the workplace
sources.limit: Workplace pathways do not establish universal effects or override conduct and context.

sources.title: Students Wearing Police Uniforms Exhibit Biased Attention toward Individuals Wearing Hoodies
sources.limit: Students were not officers; hoodie/suit images operationalized status; reaction time was not real-world behavior; no race-attention effect was found.

sources.title: Does the cowl make the monk? The effect of military and Red Cross uniforms on empathy for pain, sense of agency and moral behaviors
sources.authors: Guillaume P. Pech; Emilie A. Caspar
sources.limit: The mild-shock paradigm and temporary role clothing do not reproduce consequential professional settings.

sources.title: Uniforms, status and professional boundaries in hospital
sources.limit: One UK hospital cannot represent every health system, profession or wearer.

sources.title: Neural Basis of Professional Pride in the Reaction to Uniform Wear
sources.authors: Yeon-Ju Hong; Sunyoung Park; Sunghyon Kyeong; Jae-Jin Kim
sources.limit: Distributed task activity is not a uniform center and cannot establish that clothing caused professional pride.

sources.title: Uniform Encounter Map
sources.limit: No storage, diagnosis, bias score, authority verification or inference about another person.

sources.title: Military uniform, 1880–84
sources.limit: Material evidence of design and classification, not the wearer’s psychology.

sources.title: Uniform, late 19th century
sources.limit: Material evidence of a coordinated uniform system, not authority or competence.

sources.title: Ensemble, 1863–66
sources.limit: Military form and fashion circulation require historical context; the object is not behavioral evidence.
